quest.title: The Firework Girl's Strange Stories
quest.description: You've been in Inazuma for a while now, but your investigations continue. One day, you and Paimon arrive at the seaside...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Mora x24100, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

dialogues.speaker: Matsuzaka
dialogues.text: We're looking for the Great Mujina Youkai!

dialogues.speaker: Saika
dialogues.text: Do you know where it lives?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Great Mujina Youkai"? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuzaka
dialogues.text: Huh? You've never heard of it?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuzaka
dialogues.text: It's a sneaky monster that goes 'round playing tricks on people! It's got magic powers and can even shapeshift into anything it wants!

dialogues.speaker: Iwao
dialogues.text: One time, the Great Mujina Youkai stole some rice from our house. And this other time, it pushed my dad into the river.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a very naughty little monster!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why are you out looking for it?

dialogues.speaker: Saika
dialogues.text: 'Cause, we've finally found out how to chase it away!

dialogues.speaker: Iwao
dialogues.text: My dad said that the Great Mujina Youkai likes to play tricks on people who stay out all the time and don't come home when they're supposed to.

dialogues.speaker: Iwao
dialogues.text: So all we need to do is chase it away, then we can come out and play whenever we want!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This monster sounds scary, though... Aren't you guys afraid?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Surely your parents must be worried about you?

dialogues.speaker: Iwao
dialogues.text: Not really. I told my dad that I was going to find the Great Mujina Youkai with some friends, and he didn't even say anything.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuzaka
dialogues.text: So, we think it must be weak right now! It's probably hiding away so it can rest!

dialogues.speaker: Saika
dialogues.text: Yeah! So as long as we get home before it gets its strength back, we'll be safe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, something sounds very strange about all of this... But Paimon can't say exactly what it is...

choices.text: If a monster's coming for you, surely you won't be safe at home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Paimon feels like the Great Mujina Youkai is one of those storybook monsters that doesn't exist in the real world.

choices.text: I think so too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should tell them, so they don't waste all their time looking for it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, children, listen up! There's no need to go looking for the Great Mujina Youkai, alright? Because it isn't real.

response.speaker: Matsuzaka
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Saika
response.text: No way...

response.speaker: Iwao
response.text: That's impossible. My dad wouldn't lie to me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your folks are just worried about you, is all. They don't want you wandering too far from home, because it's too dangerous.

response.speaker: Iwao
response.text: That's not true! The Great Mujina Youkai is definitely real!

response.speaker: Matsuzaka
response.text: Yeah! Yoimiya's even making some weapons for us! And then, she's gonna show us how to blow it up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yoimiya, huh? Wait, as in... fireworks-prison-break Yoimiya?

response.speaker: Saika
response.text: We told her all about the Great Mujina Youkai. She said we shouldn't be scared of it — we should learn how to chase it away instead.

response.speaker: Matsuzaka
response.text: We've been waiting for ages now, and finally, Yoimiya said that today's the day!

response.speaker: Iwao
response.text: Uh-huh, uh-huh! Yoimiya plays with us and tells us stories all the time. She wouldn't tell a lie!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, but...

response.speaker: Iwao
response.text: Hmph! C'mon, let's get outta here and go find Yoimiya!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, hold on! Don't go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, they didn't seem to take that very well... But Paimon was only trying to look out for them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who knows what Yoimiya's got to do with this. Let's follow the kids and see what's going on.

choices.text: Guess the parents just don't want their kids staying out all the time.
We've never seen a monster like this before.
The dad's attitude doesn't quite add up...

talks.objective: Catch up to the children who are about to leave

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: #Cheer up guys, don't be so down. {F#She}{M#He} was only joking back there. How could the Great Mujina Youkai not exist, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuzaka
dialogues.text: B—But, we've never seen it for ourselves...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That's because the Great Mujina Youkai is extra powerful! And that's exactly why I need your help, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuzaka
dialogues.text: Ummmm...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's okay, don't be discouraged. Hey, remember, if you wanna be a hero, you gotta have patience — and wisdom, too.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Even if you can't find it right now, it'll definitely show up before the fireworks show starts. So remember to come and pick up your weapons from me before then, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No matter how powerful the Great Mujina Youkai might be, it's no match for my specially made fireworks! Just light 'em up and you'll scare it off, no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's up to you guys to protect your homes, your crops, and your folks!

dialogues.speaker: Matsuzaka
dialogues.text: Got it! Thanks, Miss Yoimiya, we'll try and be more patient!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, hold up a sec. I have a few slips of paper for you guys — one each. Remember to give it to your parents and tell them to keep it safe.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Just tell them it's from Yoimiya. They'll know what it's about.

dialogues.speaker: Iwao
dialogues.text: Okay! Thank you, Yoimiya! We're gonna go back now.

dialogues.speaker: Saika
dialogues.text: Thanks, Yoimiya! Come play with us soon!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Sure thing, will do! Take care on the way back, and I'll see you later!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... so...

choices.text: It's been a while.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Ah, so it WAS you guys. I guessed as much from the way the kids described you. No worries, though, I'm not blaming you.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: The Great Mujina Youkai is pretty popular with the kids, so of course they're gonna get upset if someone tries to tell them it doesn't exist.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... but it definitely doesn't exist... right?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Yeah, the first time I heard about it, I knew straight away that it was probably something the parents had come up with to stop the kids from running off all the time.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But when the kids asked me about it, I didn't wanna break it to them. I just told them that it looks cute, likes to play pranks, and doesn't hurt people.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: So I guess now, the kids' impression of the Great Mujina Youkai is mostly influenced by me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... So in a way, this monster is all a product of your creativity...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Surely it's a bad idea to keep the lie going like that?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Maybe so. In any case, I'm not gonna be the one who exposes it.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Sure, it's likely that the parents just wanted to stop the kids from staying out all the time. But they could have easily had other reasons, too.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: If I just go ahead and tell them that the Great Mujina Youkai doesn't exist without knowing the full story, then who knows — I may be doing more harm than good.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Besides, they're just kids. They should be allowed to believe it if it makes them happy. That's more important to them than questioning what's real and what isn't.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Heck, I entertain my fair share of fantasies too... The Fire Diamond that spins around and shoots out lights that are all the colors of the rainbow... Ooh — the Mist Spirits that live far off in the mountains and guide you to fairyland if you can find them...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I know that they don't really exist, but I still enjoy believing in them. If someone came up to me and starting telling me to "stop being so stupid, they don't exist, nyah nyah nyah"...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I'd give them the evil eyes and tell them to get the heck out of my face! Because... grr, it's just so annoying!

choices.text: I kind of get what you are saying.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Right!? So what if it's made up — it's also really awesome and kinda magical. So it's not up to anyone else to tell me what's what!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: The things we believed and the experiences we had when we were young turn into our priceless treasures as we grow up.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: When you were kids, surely you guys believed in things like heroes who slayed dragons, and sacred swords that cut through darkness? It's the same thing.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: If we tear apart these kids' fairy tales now, what else do we have to tell them? That Inazuma is locked down? All the grim tales of the Vision Hunt Decree? I think it's a bit too early for all of that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Yeah! Oh, way too early. For sure!

choices.text: You didn't follow that at all, did you?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Haha, whether you understood me or not, don't you worry. I'll take care of the kids, and make sure they stay safe.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Ahh! Okay, it's about time I headed back. The Naganohara Fireworks Show is just around the corner, and there's still a lot of things to get ready.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Naganohara Fireworks Show? Is that hosted by your family or something?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Well, yeah, I mean, that's why our name is on the event. It's well-known throughout Inazuma.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, on the subject — are you busy these days? If not, then you should totally come along. I'll prepare an extra-pretty firework, just for you!

choices.text: We've been looking forward to it for ages!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hee-hee, in that case, come with me to Naganohara, we'll go see my pops! There're still a few fireworks to finish off before the show.

choices.text: I'll gladly take you up on that offer.
No need to pretend to agree if you didn't understand.
Why be so childish about it?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Because maybe it doesn't matter so much if something's real or not. Maybe magic and awesomeness are what make something worth believing. Why should someone else get to take that away from you?

choices.text: We meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hey, Pops, I'm back!

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: The fireworks show is almost upon us, and the fireworks for each family are almost ready.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Oh, new faces? Who are these two? Friends, or customers?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: A bit of both, actually. They arrived in Inazuma just recently. Can't let them miss out on a fireworks show after coming all this way, can we?

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Hahaha, well, either way, come on in and have a seat and I, Naganohara Ryuunosuke, will tell you all about the long history of the Naganoharas.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That can wait. Pops, I need to ask you about something.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: A long, long time ago...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: *sigh* Pops has started telling his stories again...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Sorry about this — ever since Pops had his accident, his ears don't work too well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? But for a moment there, it almost seemed like you were having a coherent conversation...

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Much, much later, people eventually realized that if you grind certain minerals into dust, they burn with many beautiful colors.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Pops — Pops wait!

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Eh? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Did they deliver those firework materials that we ordered yet?

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Oh, yesterday's fireworks have all been delivered. So have the ones from the day before yesterday, and the ones from the day before that.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No, Pops. I meant the materials. The materials that we ordered. They should have arrived today.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Today's fireworks are almost ready, too, don't you worry! Hehe, your old man's skills are still as sharp as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No— Pops, the materials! The raw materials for making fireworks.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Sorry?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Ma-te-ri-als!

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Oh... Ohh, the materials?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes, yes! The materials!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry, sorry... Paimon got all excited because you finally got the message across, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: The materials aren't here yet. The couriers did come over to explain why, but... Well, I think they did, but I couldn't quite hear what they were saying...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No worries, as long as we know, that's fine. We can just make them later. Oh, uh — don't forget to take the goods in when they deliver them, okay, Pops?

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Of course, leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry if we were a little loud. It's always the way, though — it's like that every time I need to ask pops something.

choices.text: Still, he seems like a warm and friendly person.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Uh-huh, that's my pops! He's a good person, alright. Everyone around here respects him.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Because my pops is deaf, he never argues with anyone, and never contradicts them. He just listens cheerfully.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: When I was little, I thought it was because he really understood me, and agreed with whatever I had to say. So, I'd tell my pops everything.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Eventually, I realized that the reason he was like that was that he's deaf. But I still tell him stories every day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why would you do that?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: It just makes me happy to see him smile. And it keeps him from being lonely, right?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Anyway. More importantly right now, the fireworks show is right around the corner and the materials still haven't arrived. We need to think of an alternative...
Um, Yoimiya, is that you?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Wah! Oh, you scared me there! I thought I told you to be more careful before you speak?
S—Sorry...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hold on, I'm coming over.

choices.text: I think the two of you are quite similar.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hehe, I get told that a lot.

talks.objective: Confirm the source of the sound

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No one's looking. Okay, you can come out now. Uh, come around the side.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: *sigh* We're lucky that no one from the Tenryou Commission was around, otherwise, we'd all be in big trouble.
Sorry, I guess I was a little rash. But when I heard you come back, I just...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Sakujirou. So far, at least, everything is going according to plan.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: We're going to look for firework materials shortly. While we're out, we'll sort out the boat situation for you, as promised.

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: Thank you for all your help.

choices.text: Who is this?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: He's one of our old customers. He came back to Inazuma from the outside world not long ago. While he was smuggling himself in, the Tenryou Commission found him and put out a warrant for his arrest...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An arrest warrant!?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Shhhh, keep it down! We don't want to draw any unwanted attention.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: If Sakujirou is caught, there's no knowing what crimes they could charge him with. All we can do is find him a boat and send him out of Inazuma again.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But isn't there a thunderstorm out in the ocean?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Yeah, we know it's going to be dangerous, but there aren't many other options left.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What if the boat capsizes? Uhh! Drowning is really scary!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If things are this bad, couldn't you have just not come back in the first place?

response.speaker: Sakujirou
response.text: Well... There is something I felt I had to do...

response.speaker: Sakujirou
response.text: But as soon as I got back, I started hearing about all these unbelievable changes. I had made my mind up, originally, but now I'm not sure anymore...

response.speaker: Sakujirou
response.text: I didn't want to cause any trouble for Yoimiya or Mr. Ryuunosuke, but I'm very grateful to them for taking me in.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hey, no worries, you're more than welcome. Remember what I said? As long as you've got that little piece of paper, you'll always be a valued customer of the Naganoharas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Little piece of paper...?

choices.text: I remember something about that.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Yep, the same paper slips as the ones I gave to the kids earlier. Whenever a customer orders fireworks for a commemorative event, we always include a little paper slip with the goods.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Only people from inside my family can understand what's written on it. It's the recipe for the fireworks they ordered.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: If someone shows a Naganohara that paper slip, we guarantee we can make the exact same firework as the original one they purchased, whether it's ten or even a hundred years later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that is so awesome!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: It's a family tradition. All our regular customers know about this.

response.speaker: Sakujirou
response.text: The slip I have is from back when my parents ordered fireworks from Mr. Ryuunosuke. Now I think about it, it must be nearly 20 years ago.

response.speaker: Sakujirou
response.text: *sigh* Who would have thought that things would turn out the way they have...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: It'll be fine. Escaping in a boat is just a last resort for if there's no other way. I'll still try and come up with a different solution, because it'd be much better if you could stay in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Whatever their reasons might be, if our customers come to us looking for help, we're not about to leave them high and dry.

response.speaker: Sakujirou
response.text: Thank you... This way, I'll still have some time to consider my options...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Alright, well, let's not stay out here in the open for too long. Hurry up and get back inside. I'll let you know as soon as I have an update for you.

response.speaker: Sakujirou
response.text: Thank you, I—I'll leave it to you, then, I guess.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: *sigh* It's a shame, they still wouldn't give him a permit, even though he was born and raised in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Speaking of, you guys only got here recently, how did you manage to get a permit?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We went through a long bureaucratic process on Ritou.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even then, we only got through thanks to some help from Miss Hiiragi Chisato of the Kanjou Commission.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I see, so you had big shots helping you. I guess that won't be of much help to Sakujirou.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: *sigh* I just wish the commissions could be a little more flexible.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I bet nowhere else you've been is quite like Inazuma, huh?

choices.text: It's true.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: *sigh* Well, no matter what, I have to find a way to help him.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I'm sorry, I invited you to come and watch the fireworks, but now I have to run a few errands.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: You don't have to join me if you don't want to. I can go sort out the firework materials and the boat by myself, and then you can come and meet me back at the house later.

choices.text: I don't mind coming along.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, cool! Then let's start with Sakujirou's boat. We can chat along the way!

choices.text: I'm interested to learn how fireworks are made.
Each archon has their own idea on how to run things.
Like the paper slips you gave to the kids?
And why is he hiding in your home?

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry about me, go take care of business first. There'll always be time for my stories later.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: I have a lot of time, and a lot of stories to tell, too.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Inazuma is home to the Yae Publishing House, and a lot of people who like to write stories, too. In fact, most of what they write is based off of the kinds of fairy tales I was just talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: A bunch of them have bad endings, though. Like, oh — the Fire Diamond will get put in a rich person's gallery, where it will never be ignited again.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Or someone will see the Mist Spirit, and not manage to catch it, but because they angered it, it'll never show itself again.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The hero who slays the dragon becomes the next dragon... The sacred sword that once fought the darkness now becomes a doomsday weapon...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: *sigh* I know these kinds of stories are all the rage nowadays, but... I really can't bring myself to like them.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: If something's magical, it should be kept that way.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, if it's fine with you, can I ask how you two first met?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{F#She}{M#He} saved me from drowning this one time, and after that, we started traveling together... Why do you ask?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, nothing... I'm just quite envious of your relationship.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: If my pops had a person like you around, his being deaf wouldn't hold things up all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Why do you look so excited?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Because, because...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You said "person," and not "floating child," or "mascot"!
